blockers: The script trusts arbitrary down_argv from the spec and does not validate that it is the exact supported host-services down action tied to a retained preview identity.

Only the trace output is exclusively created before monitoring. The summary is opened exclusively after sampling and possible managed down, so a preexisting or racing summary can cause lifecycle action followed by evidence-publication failure.
memory_pressure, sysctl, and ps have no subprocess timeout. Parse/subprocess/read errors escape without a managed down attempt or a summary, so the guard is neither fail-closed nor deadline-bounded.
Candidate identity is a reusable PID only; no start time, executable, or expected process identity prevents PID-reuse misattribution.

Any existing nonempty benchmark stdout is treated as completion before process disappearance is checked. Startup output, partial output, stale output, or a crashed benchmark can therefore be reported as benchmark_completed.
The peak object combines independent extrema but retains the initial sample timestamp, so it is not a coherent timestamped peak sample.
required_before_use: Preclaim and retain exclusive descriptors for both trace and summary before the first sample.
Validate a bounded immutable spec and exact supported host-services-down argv against the retained dry-run preview.
Bound every sampling command and overall monitoring path; on sampling or parsing failure, record the error, invoke only the validated managed-down action, and publish the summary.
Bind the watched PID to stable process identity and treat identity change as disappearance.
Use benchmark process exit status and a validated final evidence artifact rather than stdout existence/size as completion.

scope: Read-only review; no model inference, download, service lifecycle, or host mutation.

focused_tests.command: .venv/bin/python scripts/run_tests.py tests/voice/test_audio_runtime.py tests/voice/test_tts_stream_config.py tests/voice/test_tts_benchmark.py tests/voice/test_voice_config.py tests/voice/test_voice_cli.py -q

findings: Unset cache limit and tracing preserve upstream defaults.
Explicit cache limits, including zero, are range checked and applied once before model load on the inference broker worker.
Memory controls require exact MLX 0.32.3 before optional runtime import.
Serial generate wrapping preserves signatures, values, iteration, close/error behavior, and worker-thread MLX access; batch and realtime omissions are documented.
Trace records include allocator values and request index but no call arguments, text, voice, reference audio, tokens, environment values, or credentials.
The preload loop is bounded to 1..3600 seconds and fails closed before readiness; actual upstream provider metadata lookup is a local cached-list operation.

tts_max_tokens.default: null/absent; request field omitted so upstream server default is retained
tts_max_tokens.parity: Manifest and candidate overlay feed the same TTSStageConfig/request builder for live pipeline and corpus benchmark; resolved benchmark evidence retains the value and hash.
tts_max_tokens.validation: Boolean, fractional, zero, negative, string, and values above 8192 are rejected.
